deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is the outer (address) side of a folded sheet that served as a wrapper or cover. In the centre-right, written in pencil in Kurrent script, is the address 'Herrn Professor Riemann / Hochwohlgeboren' ('To Professor Riemann, Esq.'). A small pencil mark resembling a cross or 't' sits below 'Herrn'. Across the central fold is an oval ink stamp of the Göttingen bookseller 'DEUERLICH'SCHE BUCHHANDLUNG * GÖTTINGEN *'. This suggests the sheet came to Riemann as a bookseller's wrapper or delivery cover, perhaps holding a book, an invoice or a parcel. Later archival hands added '[1 Bl]' ('1 sheet') at the top, the foliation '76', and a bracketed number '(118c.)' or '(1186.)'. The faint ruled rectangles visible through the paper are the floor plans drawn on the verso, the next page, which are labelled in dialect German: 'kamer', 'stuben', 'küche', 'tür', 'of' (Ofen, stove), 'pet' (Bett, bed), 'tisch'. Those plans are domestic and architectural sketches of rooms, perhaps for apartment hunting or furniture arrangement, not mathematics. The page bears only on biography: it shows Riemann was a customer of the Deuerlich bookshop and reused wrapper paper for scratch work. The 'Professor' title dates it to 1857 or later, when he became außerordentlicher Professor.
